page: Microsoft Azure D128alds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 64 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system contains 256 GB of RAM, resulting in a 2 GB per core allocation tailored for compute-heavy operations. The hardware includes 7,560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and the CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI. The server operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-decile performance across multi-core computing and memory operations. The instance records a multi-core stress-ng score of 233,738.78 and a PassMark CPU mark of 134,326.25. Memory bandwidth reaches 376.33 GB/sec on large read blocks and 197.42 GB/sec on write blocks. For high-throughput services, it achieves 200.09 million Redis SET operations per second and 105.54 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference benchmarks also confirm top-tier throughput for small, medium, and large text processing tasks.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the hardware configuration optimizes processing density while limiting memory capacity relative to core count. The bundling of 7,560 GB of direct NVMe SSD space delivers high I/O throughput without requiring reliance on external storage arrays for scratch data. This configuration delivers strong resource density for concurrent execution pipelines, batch data transformations, in-memory caching nodes, large software compilation, and parallel web serving clusters.
description: Microsoft Azure D128alds_v7 is a high-density, compute-oriented instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 128 dedicated vCPUs over 64 physical cores alongside 256 GB of memory and 7,560 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The platform features advanced instruction extensions, including AVX-512 and VAES, but contains no discrete GPUs. Across stress-ng multi-core testing, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and memory bandwidth evaluations, the server consistently achieves top-tier results. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio prioritizes raw compute capacity over expansive memory footprints, complemented by extensive high-speed local disk capacity. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation, batch data transformation, high-throughput Redis caching, web serving, and CPU-bound model inference.
